A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARTIST in Adaptive Time Series Reasoning via Segment Selection. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison. Retained equations, tables, and figures can be matched across relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on six time-series reasoning benchmarks, component ablations in Table 3, and data-utilization analyses in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds modality, adaptive-search, computational-cost, long-sequence, and localization evaluations in its appendices.

M1.justification: The controller-reasoner procedure, rewards, and hierarchical optimizer remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a limited architectural and input adaptation: an SFT-only ARTIST variant using Qwen2.5-VL-3B and rendered plots instead of Qwen3-4B and tokenized time-series inputs.

E1.justification: The six original benchmarks remain. Appendix K adds FreqShape and SeqCombSingle for evaluating localization against ground-truth masks, extending the evaluated task coverage. Appendix J adds a distinct long-input scenario using RCW sequences extended from 4,000 to 8,000 and 12,000 timesteps.

E2.justification: v2 retains the original comparators and adds an adapted PixelReasoner comparison on ECG-QA and TimeX/TimeX++ comparisons on the two synthetic localization benchmarks. This substantially broadens comparisons to adaptive search and dedicated explainability methods. PixelReasoner was cited, but not evaluated, in v1.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce an SFT-only vision-backbone comparison, inference timing aggregated over eight runs, and RCW extension through noisy tiled copies without retraining. Appendix K adds mask binarization at 0.5, temporal tolerances of ±5/±10, localization metrics, and five-fold evaluation on a shared 200-sample test subset. The original benchmark protocols remain documented.

E4.justification: The original component ablations, utilization analysis, and case studies are retained. New analyses investigate the Sleep-QA modality bottleneck, robustness to longer inputs, agreement between selected segments and ground-truth evidence, and training/inference costs. These substantially extend diagnostic and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight independent runs for the original evaluations. v2 additionally reports five-fold cross-validation and mean ± standard deviation for region-level localization results in Tables 10–11; the segment-level rows contain point estimates. This adds uncertainty reporting without establishing increased runs for existing results.

E6.justification: The original scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New results include 65.00% Sleep-QA accuracy for vision-based ARTIST versus 28.13% for tokenized ARTIST and 47.51% for TimeMaster in Appendix G's SFT-only comparison. Table 7 adds PixelReasoner at 60.15% versus ARTIST at 69.81% on ECG-QA. Further tables add cost, extended-length, and localization outcomes, including mixed rankings against TimeX/TimeX++.

T1.justification: Appendix K introduces task-specific evaluation definitions, especially Sufficient Evidence Rate: covering consecutive spike clusters for FreqShape and all discriminative subsequences for SeqCombSingle. The ARTIST mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(20) remain unchanged; no new theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: question-adaptive segment selection, hierarchical collaborative RL, and superiority on the original six benchmarks with the reported 6.46-point average accuracy advantage. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an asserted modality-based explanation for the Sleep-QA gap, a segment-cost explanation for long-sequence stability, and interpretations of complementary localization strengths versus explainability methods. It retains the univariate and irregular-sampling limitations, connects inference overhead to measured costs, and explicitly leaves vision-based SFT+RL to future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds project/code links, clarifies that SFT baselines use ARTIST's training data, and discloses SFT parameter counts, batch size, hardware, convergence, training times, GPU-hours, and inference-timing conditions. Appendix E.1 also reports around 100 RL updates while Appendix E retains one epoch; these conflicting descriptions do not establish an actual budget change.

R1.justification: A new related-work subsection substantially develops the relationship to dynamic visual search, adding works such as ZoomEye, Chain-of-Spot, Set-of-Mark, DetToolChain, and DeepEyes and explaining differences in supervision and temporal context. Appendix K adds positioning against TimeX and TimeX++. PixelReasoner's publication update and duplicate-reference cleanup are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 makes localized abstract and reward-description edits, adds equal-contribution and publication/disclosure text, and extends the structure with a related-work subsection, Appendix E.1, and Appendices G–K. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables, including resource-cost displays and paired region/tolerance-based localization tables. Figures 1–4 and the original tables retain their content, with several relocated through reflow; Table 3 now appears below Figure 4. The substantial change is the expanded tabular presentation.

improvement.justification: Tables 10–11 address v1's lack of quantitative ground-truth validation of segment selection, Table 7 adds an adaptive-search comparator, and Tables 5/8 make computational tradeoffs measurable. These substantially strengthen support for the central mechanism and practical transparency. Limitations remain: the modality study also changes backbone, the length test keeps relevant evidence in a fixed prefix, and RL-budget descriptions conflict. These restrict some new interpretations but do not outweigh the substantive gains.
